chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the coitus interruptus, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is up to the man; he can place it (seed) wherever he so desires.'

key_terms.إِلَى الرَّجُلِ: Up to the man / Discretion of the man
key_terms.الْعَزْلِ: Coitus interruptus (withdrawal of semen before ejaculation)
key_terms.يَصْرِفُهُ: He can direct/place it (referring to the semen)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on coitus interruptus (al-'azl) and who has the authority to decide?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of 'al-'azl' (coitus interruptus) by affirming the husband's discretionary authority to withdraw semen before ejaculation. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the husband's right to control this aspect of marital intimacy, provided it does not cause harm or violate the wife's rights, reflecting the principle of mutual consent and flexibility in marital relations.
